The five profile refusals in front of it -- non-positive size, the ValidCubeFormats list, MaxCubeSize 512, the unconditional NonPow2Cube rule and the DXT alignment -- are managed and never reach a route. |
| TextureCube face data transfer | VERIFIED_NATIVE_ON_OPENGLES3 | Cna_texturecube_set_data and cna_texturecube_get_data round-trip all six faces on OPENGLES3 and answer CNA_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED for all six on HEADLESS, which CNA's header names a legitimate outcome ('unsupported storage returns NOT_SUPPORTED atomically'). Foundation64VolumeTextureTests asserts whichever the renderer does in full -- every face refused naming the route, or every face read back exactly -- and every XNA validation in front of the transfer. |
| Texture3D on this profile | VERIFIED_MANAGED | No Texture3D can be constructed on a Reach device and that is XNA's rule: ValidateCreationParameters raises ProfileFeatureNotSupported when MaxVolumeExtent is zero, and the table extracted from the pinned assembly gives Reach a zero extent and an empty ValidVolumeFormats. The type is complete and implemented, unreachable on this profile rather than absent. CNA agrees independently -- cna_texture3d_create answers NOT_SUPPORTED -- but the refusal raised is the managed one, not the native result code. |
| RenderTargetCube creation and binding | VERIFIED_NATIVE | Cna_render_target_cube_create answers a game-child handle and cna_graphics_device_set_render_target_cube binds each of the six faces, inside a live LoadContent callback. RenderTargetCube reads cna_render_target_get_info, which answers the real extents, level count, format, depth format, sample count and usage. Under CNA 0.21 cna_texturecube_get_info answered a render-target-cube handle with SUCCESS and zeros (SW-07); CNA 0.35 answers it correctly (cna/build-probe/qual-probes/sw-graphics.c). |
| Multiple render targets | VERIFIED_NATIVE_WITH_MEASURED_XNA_DIVERGENCE | Cna_graphics_device_set_render_targets binds an array, cna_graphics_device_get_render_target_count answers its length and cna_graphics_device_copy_render_targets hands back each binding's handle, array slice and face -- measured for one 2D target, one cube face and TWO DISTINCT 2D targets (build-probe/f65_rtcube.c). The artifact accepts two; XNA does not, because Reach's MaxRenderTargets is 1, so the projection refuses at two with ProfileMaxRenderTargets and the native capability is never reached. CNA's own refusals were measured too and all three are documented: a duplicate target was INTERNAL under CNA 0.21 and is INVALID_ARGUMENT under 0.35 ('the same render target cannot be bound to more than one slot'; the projection refuses first with XNA's CannotSetAlreadyUsedRenderTarget), a nonzero array_slice on a 2D target is NOT_SUPPORTED, and a non-positive-X face on a 2D target is INVALID_ARGUMENT. |
| Render-target binding readback | VERIFIED_MANAGED | GetRenderTargets hands back the managed RenderTargetBinding values that were bound, from a cache on RuntimeState. CNA can say which native handle occupies each slot but publishes no route from a native object back to a handle, so object identity -- which XNA's Array.Copy of currentRenderTargetBindings gives -- can only come from a cache. cna_graphics_device_copy_render_targets corroborates the handles and faces and is deliberately not bound: no projected member consumes it. |
| Runtime lifetime with a bound resource | MEASURED_NATIVE_DIVERGENCE | A GraphicsResource holds its GraphicsDevice facade strongly and the facade holds the RuntimeState strongly, so any cache on the runtime that holds a resource closes RuntimeState -> resource -> facade -> RuntimeState. Foundation 63 added the first such cache and binding one vertex buffer kept the runtime, every native handle it tracks and every registered child alive past Game.Dispose for the life of the process. RuntimeState.invalidateAfterNativeShutdown now releases every cache that holds a resource, which is also what XNA's GraphicsDevice.Dispose does. A retain cycle is invisible to AddressSanitizer; RuntimeLifetimeTests is what asks, with two controls proving the measurement can observe a released runtime at all. |
| Texture sampler slots | VERIFIED_NATIVE | Cna_graphics_device_set_texture and _get_texture bind and read all 16 slots of both shader stages inside a live callback, and CNA_TextureSlotInfo::bound distinguishes 'occupied by something no handle names' from 'empty' (build-probe/f66_slots.c). The refusals were measured too: slot 16 is INVALID_ARGUMENT 'The texture sampler slot is out of range', an unknown stage is INVALID_ARGUMENT 'The shader stage is not recognized', and a texture that is the active render target is INVALID_STATE 'A texture that is currently bound as a render target cannot be bound for sampling' -- which is CNA's own version of XNA's MustResolveRenderTarget, reached only if the managed check were removed. Destroying a bound texture succeeds and empties every slot it held. |
| Texture collection slot counts | VERIFIED_MANAGED | RESOLVES the divergence recorded for the sampler collections. All four collections -- Textures, VertexTextures, SamplerStates and VertexSamplerStates -- are sized from the device's own profile: MaxSamplers 16 and MaxVertexSamplers 0 under Reach, 16 and 4 under HiDef, from the table extracted in Foundation 62. Until then all four were 16 long because the binding had no profile to ask, and a 16-slot vertex collection accepted fifteen indices XNA raises ArgumentOutOfRangeException for. CNA's own limit is the wider of the two -- CNA_TEXTURE_COLLECTION_MAX_TEXTURES is 16 on both stages -- and XNA's profile is the narrower rule that decides. |
| Effect creation and application | VERIFIED_NATIVE | Cna_effect_create_empty builds what CNA's header calls 'the minimal concrete adapter for the native abstract Effect base class' -- no parameters, one technique, one pass, and a native type name that is literally Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.Effect. cna_effect_apply and cna_effect_pass_apply both succeed, and after either the same cna_graphics_device_draw_primitives that answered CNA_RESULT_INTERNAL with 'no effect has been applied' returns 0 (build-probe/f67_effect.c). That is the claim Foundation 63 withheld the whole draw family on, now tested in both directions. effect_has_renderer and effect_get_is_compiled_ext are both false on HEADLESS and neither prevents apply. |
| Effect object-graph identity | VERIFIED_MANAGED | Cna_effect_get_techniques hands back a fresh OWNED collection view on every call and get_at a fresh element view, so without a cache effect.Techniques !== effect.Techniques and technique.Passes[0] !== technique.Passes[0]. XNA holds a List<T> built once and indexes into it, so identity holds there; EffectElementCache reproduces that by caching per index. The five ..._collection_find routes are deliberately NOT bound for the same reason: find answers a second owned view of the element rather than the one get_at gave, so a name lookup would break the identity the index path establishes. XNA's own Item[String] is a managed scan over its List<T>, which is what this does. |
| Vertex buffer draw range | MEASURED_NATIVE_DIVERGENCE | CNA counts vertices WRITTEN, not capacity allocated: a 64-vertex buffer with a renderer, bound, with an effect applied, refuses every draw with CNA_RESULT_INVALID_ARGUMENT and 'The requested primitive range exceeds the bound vertex buffer'; uploading data makes the identical call succeed (build-probe/f67_effect.c). XNA has no such rule -- an un-SetData'd VertexBuffer draws undefined contents rather than raising. The draw members must decide explicitly what to do about it; a test that happened to upload data first would never have seen it, and the probe found it only because its first draft misread the refusal as a capacity problem. |
| Draw validation ownership | VERIFIED_MANAGED | The managed half of every draw is reproduced and is what the tests assert: the disposal check, MustDrawSomething for a non-positive primitiveCount, ProfileMaxPrimitiveCount against the extracted limit (65,535 on Reach), NumberVerticesMustBeGreaterZero BEFORE the primitive count on the indexed draws, NonZeroInstanceFrequency on the three non-instanced ones, InvalidInstanceStreams on the instanced one when the bound streams are all instanced or all not, and the user-primitive draws' seven tests including the unsigned offset-plus-element-count bound. VerifyCanDraw's eight messages are recorded native-owned: five read shader state outright, and three -- ProfileInvalidBlendFormat, ProfileInvalidFilterFormat, ProfileNoWrapNonPow2 -- LOOK derivable from the pinned profile table but decide on the D3D tracker's applied sampler state and bound textures, which canonical CNA code changes without this binding seeing it. A check reading a partial view would silently not fire. |
| BinaryReader and uncompressed XNB content reading | VERIFIED_MANAGED | ContentReader is a real subclass of the demand-driven .NET Framework 4.0 BinaryReader projection. Independent bytes verify explicit little-endian primitives, signedness, seven-bit UTF-8 strings, UTF-16 character units, EOF/short reads, BaseStream identity and deterministic close. A byte-authored Windows XNB v5 fixture passes through public ContentManager.Load, the type-reader manifest, typed/erased generic bridges, one-based reader IDs, deferred shared-resource fixups, relative external references, cache identity and disposal registration. The semantically unrelated cna_content_reader_* save-game routes are deliberately unbound. |
| Compressed XNB content reading | UNSUPPORTED_EXPLICITLY | The managed header path recognizes the XNA 4.0 compressed flag and raises the pinned decompression failure. No LZX decompressor is admitted by this selected closure, and no claim is made for LZX or non-XNA LZ4 content; uncompressed XNB remains fully testable without a native library. |
| ResourceManager-backed XNB content reading | VERIFIED_MANAGED | The selected self-contained ResourceManager projection provides virtual invariant-culture GetObject/GetString lookup, BaseName, IgnoreCase, ResourceSetType and ReleaseAllResources. ResourceContentManager obtains project-owned byte resources through that virtual GetObject path and feeds the same managed ContentReader/XNB pipeline; CNA's similarly named placeholder route is deliberately unbound. Assembly, CultureInfo, ResourceSet and UnmanagedMemoryStream overloads remain outside the measured closure. |

99 operations. The machine-readable source is
`docs/runtime-capabilities.json`.
